source_name: RTCG — Ekonomija (national public broadcaster)
why_relevant: Public-service broadcaster's economy desk: reliable, non-paywalled record of official announcements (CBCG, ministries, state-linked bank projects). Good corroboration layer and free to archive.

source_name: Naslovi.net — Montenegrin/regional headline aggregator
why_relevant: Cross-outlet aggregator that indexes sr-language headlines by date and source, including Montenegrin coverage (confirmed: TIPS Clone launch item aggregating Slobodna Evropa). Ideal low-cost discovery layer to find outlets and articles a per-site crawler would miss, and to detect which outlets republish a given wire item.

source_name: Antena M (antenam.net) — economy/finance coverage
why_relevant: Second-tier Montenegrin portal that nonetheless carried substantive coverage of CBCG reform (Austrian National Bank support for SEPA and TIPS Clone). Useful as breadth/corroboration and occasionally publishes items other outlets skip.

source_name: Aktuelno.me — economy/finance coverage
why_relevant: Smaller Montenegrin portal carrying IFI-financing stories (confirmed: EIB investment totals in Montenegro since independence). IFI financing frequently funds bank/state digital infrastructure, so these items are leading indicators of upcoming procurement.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL) — Balkan service, Montenegro payments coverage
why_relevant: Regional sr-language outlet that covers Montenegrin payments infrastructure in a comparative Western-Balkans frame (confirmed piece on EU instant payments introduced in Montenegro and BiH). Valuable for cross-market context that purely domestic outlets lack.

source_name: B92 Biz — Region desk (Serbian outlet covering Montenegro banking)
why_relevant: Serbian business desk that republishes Montenegrin banking/payments stories (confirmed instant-payments item). Useful redundancy when Montenegrin originals are paywalled or bot-defended, and shows which ME stories carry regional weight.

source_name: Sjever CG (sjevercg.me) — regional business/partnership coverage
why_relevant: Northern-Montenegro regional outlet; carried the same 'Partnerstvo koje pokreće uspjeh' partnership piece as CdM, illustrating that bank PR/partnership copy is syndicated across small regional portals. Useful for detecting the PR distribution footprint of a vendor or bank campaign.

source_name: Council of Europe — Analysis of the media sector in Montenegro
why_relevant: A mapped inventory of Montenegrin media with ownership and reach, in sr. This is the meta-source for completing the outlet inventory for this cell and for assessing each outlet's independence and likely PR-capture — directly informing credibility scoring.

source_name: Ahrefs competitor listings for Montenegrin news domains
why_relevant: Traffic-competitor listings for pobjeda.me and standard.co.me enumerate peer Montenegrin news domains by audience overlap — a mechanical way to discover sr-language outlets this cell has not yet inventoried, independent of what search engines surface.

source_name: Payten (ASEE payments arm) — regional payments/POS/acquiring site
why_relevant: Payten is the dominant regional card/POS/ATM services provider serving Montenegrin banks (e.g. NLB Smart POS Montenegro is a Payten-built app, package com.payten.nlb.podgorica). Its country pages and product pages are the main disclosure surface for ME acquiring/terminal footprint — Printec's most direct competitor set.

source_name: Google Play / App Store developer listings of regional vendors (ASEE, Payten, ABC Tech Group) for ME bank apps
why_relevant: App package IDs leak the vendor behind a Montenegrin bank's digital channel even when no press release exists: 'hr.asseco.android.jimba.nlbcrnagoracorp.me' (ASEE, Croatia entity, NLB CG corporate), 'mne.asseco.android.ae.nlbmne' (NLB Klik CG), 'com.payten.nlb.podgorica' (NLB Smart POS CG), 'com.abctechgroup.adriatic' (Adriatic Bank mBanking). This is the cheapest reliable vendor-to-ME-bank mapping available.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin/regional banking news portal (Crna Gora bankarstvo category)
why_relevant: Although .me-domiciled, it covers the ex-Yu banking space as one territory and republishes regional group announcements (NLB, OTP, Intesa, Addiko) that touch ME subsidiaries; a bridge between the regional spillover cell and local reporting.

source_name: Netokracija (RS/HR editions) — regional tech/fintech media
why_relevant: Regional tech trade press covering vendor product launches, fintech partnerships and integrator hiring across RS/HR/BA; frequently the only place a regional integrator's Adriatic banking win is described in technical detail, including ME subsidiaries.

source_name: Comtrade System Integration — Banking & Finance practice (Belgrade) + Comtrade IT Solutions and Services d.o.o. Podgorica
source_subtype: vendor corporate site + company registry entry
why_relevant: Serbian integrator with a registered Podgorica entity; core-banking modernization, open banking and analytics offering means it competes for ME bank projects delivered from Belgrade. Registration record at the Montenegrin Chamber of Commerce confirms the local vehicle for a regionally-run business.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — business directory of foreign-owned IT subsidiaries
why_relevant: Chamber-of-commerce member records reveal which regional integrators actually maintain a Montenegrin legal vehicle (vs. serving ME purely from Belgrade/Zagreb), giving a defensible list of who is present on the ground.

source_name: NLB Group corporate site — group markets / NLB Banka Podgorica pages
why_relevant: Classic group-level spillover source: NLB runs one digital-channel stack (NLB Klik, NLB ProKlik, NLB Smart POS) across six markets and rolls it into its Montenegrin subsidiary. Group IR/news pages announce technology programmes before the ME subsidiary ever mentions them.

source_name: OTP Group / CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka) — group-to-subsidiary technology disclosures
why_relevant: CKB is the largest ME bank and an OTP Group member; OTP standardises card/POS and digital platforms regionally (OTP Serbia, OTP HR, CKB), so CKB's terminal and channel technology is usually decided in Budapest/Belgrade/Zagreb. CKB product pages document the POS/acquiring set-up actually in market.

source_name: Global vendor customer-success libraries with ME bank entries (e.g. Qualys case study on Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka)
why_relevant: Demonstrates the pattern that ME bank references are published on the vendor's global/EMEA site, not locally. Vendor case-study libraries (security, core banking, cards, ATM) are therefore a primary discovery channel for who supplies Montenegrin banks — usually via a regional Adriatic partner named in the text.

source_name: Combis (Hrvatski Telekom / Deutsche Telekom group) — Croatian regional ICT integrator
why_relevant: Zagreb-based integrator operating across SEE and owned by HT; the Crnogorski Telekom sister-company relationship inside Deutsche Telekom gives it a natural channel into Montenegrin enterprise/banking infrastructure work run from Croatia.

source_name: KING ICT — Croatian systems integrator (SEE footprint)
why_relevant: Large Zagreb integrator that bids regional public-sector and financial-sector ICT tenders; a plausible supplier to ME banks and state financial institutions with the reference filed on the Croatian site only.

source_name: ABC Tech Group — regional digital-banking software house (Adriatic Bank mBanking developer)
why_relevant: Identified as the developer behind Adriatic Bank Podgorica's mobile banking app (package com.abctechgroup.adriatic) — a concrete instance of a regionally-based software house holding a Montenegrin bank reference that is invisible on ME domains.

source_name: Biznis u regionu — regional (ex-Yu) business/banking news aggregator
why_relevant: Explicitly regional editorial framing (RS/BA/ME/HR/MK as one market) with tag pages for central banks and payment topics; useful for catching ME items that regional vendors and bank groups place in regional press.

source_name: Adria TV Portal — regional (Adriatic) news portal, economy section
why_relevant: Adriatic-framed outlet that carried Montenegrin instant-payments coverage; representative of the regional-media layer where ME payments-infrastructure milestones are reported for a cross-border audience.

source_name: ICT Cortex (ME ICT cluster) — bridge between regional vendors and ME banking demand
why_relevant: Montenegrin ICT cluster publishing analysis of fintech/banking transformation and listing member firms, many of which are subcontractors or local arms of regional integrators — a way to map who actually delivers regional vendors' ME work.

source_name: LinkedIn company/job pages of regional integrators and ME bank subsidiaries
why_relevant: Job ads and employee-post announcements from Belgrade/Zagreb/Sarajevo delivery teams often name the Montenegrin client or the platform being rolled out into the ME subsidiary before any press release exists.

source_name: Entrust / global technology partner directories listing Asseco and regional partners
why_relevant: Partner directories of global card/security/ATM vendors reveal which regional (RS/HR/BA) firms hold reseller or implementation rights for the Adriatic territory including Montenegro — mapping the indirect channel that covers ME.

source_name: Kraft NT (Podgorica) — local payment-terminal / Android payment application reseller
why_relevant: Local Podgorica reseller of payment terminals and Android payment applications — the typical last-mile partner through which a regional vendor's terminal estate reaches Montenegrin merchants; directly competitive-relevant to Printec.
